headline: TECK-BACKED ABRASILVER HITS 748m AT 0.69% Cu AT LA COIPITA — NEW YARETAS SUR TARGET ADDS 42m AT 1.03% Cu IN ARGENTINA PORPHYRY
source_name: Investing News Network / AbraSilver Resource Corp. (TSX: ABRA)
snippet: AbraSilver Resource Corp. (TSX: ABRA) reported June 15, 2026 assay results from its 2026 drill program at the La Coipita copper-gold-molybdenum project in San Juan Province, Argentina — with hole DDH-LC26-010 returning the strongest intercept yet drilled at the project: 747.5 metres at 0.69% copper, 0.06 g/t gold, and 142 ppm molybdenum from the Yaretas target, confirming the vertical continuity of a large-scale porphyry system. A new discovery at the Yaretas Sur target (42 metres at 1.03% copper, 0.63 g/t gold, and 41 g/t silver) establishes mineralization in previously undrilled ground and materially expands the known copper footprint. The 5,248-metre, 7-hole 2026 program is fully funded and operated by Teck Resources Limited under an earn-in and joint venture agreement — Teck has invested approximately US$23 million across 19 holes and 11,270 metres to date. With copper above $4.50/lb and the US Commerce Department's June 30 copper tariff assessment approaching, a Tier 1 partner-backed porphyry at scale in Argentina represents one of the most financially de-risked junior copper exploration narratives currently active on the TSX.

headline: CHINA RARE EARTH PRICE INDEX CLIMBS TO 252.8 — DYSPROSIUM UP 105% YTD AT $930/kg AS HEAVY REE BIFURCATION WIDENS
snippet: China's Rare Earth Price Index (CREI) reached 252.8 as of June 15, 2026 — approximately 153% above its 2010 baseline — with heavy rare earth elements (HREEs) leading the advance even as neodymium-praseodymium (NdPr) corrected roughly 21% from its April peak before recovering. Dysprosium metal held near $930.70 per kilogram (up 105% year-to-date, up 163% since January 2025) with terbium oxide quoted at ¥7,650–7,850/kg domestically and as much as five times higher in ex-China retail markets — a bifurcation driven by the MOFCOM Announcement No. 18 licensing framework that gates HREE exports through a slow, discretionary government approval process. The divergence between the NdPr headline correction and persistent HREE strength tracks a structural supply concentration reality: the NdFeB magnet grades specified for EV traction motors and humanoid robot actuators in high-temperature operating environments (H, SH, UH, EH series) require dysprosium or terbium additions that have no cost-effective substitute. For junior rare earth investors, the CREI at 252.8 with HREE prices outpacing NdPr is the clearest signal yet that projects with meaningful dysprosium and terbium content in their resource estimates carry a valuation premium that TREO-focused models systematically understate.

headline: GREAT PACIFIC GOLD ADVANCES TWO-RIG CAMPAIGN AT WILD DOG — 7 HOLES DRILLED AT KAVASUKI ACROSS 15km EPITHERMAL CORRIDOR IN PNG
snippet: Great Pacific Gold Corp. (TSXV: GPAC) provided a June 15, 2026 exploration update for its Wild Dog Project on the island of New Britain, Papua New Guinea, confirming both diamond drill rigs are active: one at Kavasuki (holes KVH-01 through KVH-07 completed along an east-west cross-section of the north-south trending epithermal vein corridor, with assays for KVH-06 and KVH-07 pending) and a second rig at the Kasie Ridge target. The Wild Dog structural corridor stretches 15 kilometres in strike length with interpreted depth extent of over 1,000 metres, established through historical exploration, 2025 MobileMT geophysics, and LiDAR surveys. New Britain hosts some of the Pacific Rim's most productive high-sulphidation and intermediate-sulphidation epithermal gold systems; the two-rig program reflects a systematic district-scale exploration campaign rather than a single-target test, with the H2 2026 drill schedule outlined in today's release designed to advance the most promising vectors before the next assay-driven news cycle.

headline: GSP RESOURCE TURNS FIRST 2026 DRILL AT HIGHLAND VALLEY — PORPHYRY COPPER AT MER AND 5.04 g/t Au FOLLOW-UP AT ALWIN, BC
source_name: Junior Mining Network / GSP Resource Corp. (TSXV: GSPR)
snippet: GSP Resource Corp. (TSXV: GSPR) announced June 15, 2026 that Phase 1 drilling has commenced at the combined Alwin-Mer properties in British Columbia's Highland Valley Copper Camp — Canada's largest producing copper district and home to Teck Resources' Highland Valley Copper Mine — with the 1,200–1,500 metre program targeting porphyry copper potential at the Mer property and high-grade gold expansion at Alwin. The Alwin target follows up on discovery hole AM-24-06 (drilled late 2024), which returned 5.04 g/t gold and 1.01% copper over 7.90 metres — a grade-thickness result in the Highland Valley context that attracted investor attention given proximity to established infrastructure. The Mer porphyry copper target is receiving its first-ever systematic drill test, with surface results and geological mapping identifying a porphyry-style target in a district where large-scale copper deposits are known to occur. Phase 1 results are expected to guide a Phase 2 scope decision ahead of the fall 2026 season.

headline: FX LEADERS: GOLD EYES $4,450 BREAKOUT INTO WARSH'S DEBUT FOMC — 97% HOLD PRICED, DOT PLOT IS THE REAL BINARY
snippet: FX Leaders' June 15, 2026 gold price analysis identifies $4,450 per ounce as the immediate technical breakout target heading into the June 16–17 FOMC meeting — Kevin Warsh's debut as Fed Chair — with the Iran ceasefire having cleared the primary macro headwind and CME FedWatch pricing a 97% probability of a rate hold. The analytical key: the rate decision is effectively settled, but Warsh's first dot plot — the FOMC's forward rate projections — is where real information content lies. If the median projection shifts to show two hikes in 2026 (upgrading the December hike probability from 70% to something higher), gold's $4,450 target stalls. If the language softens or the median holds, $4,450 becomes the first resistance level en route to the institutional year-end targets that Goldman Sachs ($5,400), JPMorgan (~$6,000), UBS ($5,500), and Morgan Stanley ($5,200) maintain 25–44% above current prices. For junior gold mining investors managing entry into the current recovery leg, a weekly close above $4,450 post-FOMC is the specific technical signal that separates continued accumulation from reassessment.

headline: CHINA GOLD ETFs LOG FIRST MONTHLY OUTFLOWS SINCE AUGUST 2025 — RMB8.2B EXITS IN MAY AS PBOC KEEPS BUYING AT EVERY LEVEL
snippet: Chinese gold exchange-traded funds recorded net outflows of RMB8.2 billion ($1.2 billion) in May 2026 — their first monthly outflows since August 2025, ending an eight-month inflow streak — as local equity market strength diverted retail investor capital and the Shanghai Gold Benchmark PM fell 2.7% on the month, according to the World Gold Council's June 12 China market update. Total holdings fell 8.3 tonnes to 293 tonnes by May 31 as assets under management dropped 5% to RMB289 billion. The structural divergence is the key signal: China's People's Bank of China maintained its multi-year official reserve accumulation programme through May despite the retail ETF liquidation — confirming that sovereign institutional demand treated the $4,150–$4,218 price band as a structural floor rather than a level requiring reassessment. For TSXV and ASX mining investors, the WGC data provides a concrete validation of the June floor: the retail ETF outflows happened precisely in the zone that analysts and central bank buyers defended, making the Iran ceasefire-driven recovery from those levels more structurally durable than the retail sentiment data alone would suggest.

headline: AI DATA CENTERS LIFT URANIUM TERM PRICE TO $91.50/lb — META COMMITS TO 6.6 GWe NUCLEAR AS 38 NATIONS PLEDGE TRIPLE CAPACITY
snippet: The long-term uranium contract price has climbed to $91.50 per pound — a $5.50 premium to the current $86/lb spot — as hyperscale AI data center operators add new structural demand for nuclear baseload power that has no precedent in prior uranium cycles. Meta Platforms has committed to securing up to 6.6 gigawatts of new nuclear capacity; Microsoft, Amazon, and Alphabet have made parallel commitments, with the four major AI hyperscalers guiding collectively to over $710 billion in 2026 capital expenditure that includes significant long-duration nuclear procurement. The $91.50 term price premium to spot is the market's forward signal: utilities and industrial buyers are locking in long-term supply above the current spot price, the classic early-stage contango pattern that has preceded rapid spot price recoveries in prior uranium cycles. For TSXV and ASX uranium developers, the term-price leadership — combined with 38 nations pledging to triple nuclear capacity by 2050 and the approaching 2028 US Russian uranium import ban deadline — establishes a multi-layered demand case that transforms the $86 spot price from a consolidation point into the floor of a structurally ascending price environment.

headline: LITHIUM HOLDS AT ¥170,500/t AS CATL JIANXIAWO SUSPENSION AND ZIMBABWE EXPORT CURBS UNDERPIN FLOOR
snippet: Global lithium carbonate prices held at approximately ¥170,500 per tonne ($25.21/kg) as of June 14, 2026, consolidating following Q1's near-doubling to a $26,278/tonne peak in battery-grade lithium carbonate. Two supply-side factors are maintaining the price floor: the ongoing suspension of CATL's Jianxiawo mine in Jiangxi Province (triggered by licence expiry in August 2025, with no confirmed restart date) and Zimbabwe's export restrictions on lithium ore, which collectively offset the supply impact of Australian mine restarts at Core Lithium's Finniss Project and Mineral Resources' Bald Hill operation. Speculative long positioning has cooled after exchange authority interventions raised margin requirements — a technical reset that has historically preceded the next demand-driven leg higher. China's commitment to double national EV charging infrastructure to 180 gigawatts provides the demand-side anchor that TSXV and ASX lithium brine developers can reference when presenting pre-feasibility study economics: Beijing's infrastructure commitment creates forward ordering visibility that makes Argentine brine project timelines (2027–2028 PFS-to-production) directly relevant to active government procurement planning.

headline: KITCO: GOLD'S HORMUZ RALLY IS MORE BULLISH THAN A SAFE-HAVEN BID — OIL-SHOCK INFLATION RISK FLIPS TO RATE-RELIEF AND DIESEL COST TAILWIND
snippet: Kitco's June 15, 2026 AM report frames the Strait of Hormuz peace deal rally in analytical terms that distinguish it from typical geopolitical-resolution pullbacks: the mechanism is not safe-haven demand removal (which is gold-negative) but rather the conversion of an oil-shock inflation premium into a monetary-easing tailwind. With oil falling below $100/barrel, the 70% probability of a December 2026 FOMC hike — priced into futures markets while Iran risk kept energy inflation elevated — is being directly unwound, removing the primary rate-path headwind to gold's recovery from the $4,150–$4,218 support zone. The dual channel makes this categorically different: higher gold spot prices and lower miner diesel costs (fuel represents 15–20% of open-pit cash expenses) are moving simultaneously in the same direction for the first time since January 2026. Gold at $4,336 and silver at $70.67 were firmer in early US trading on the session, with the Kitco analysis pointing to Wednesday's FOMC dot plot as the sequential confirmation event: if Warsh softens the December hike language, the Iran ceasefire rate-relief mechanism gets a second-order amplification that extends the recovery leg toward $4,600.

headline: NdPr CORRECTS 21% IN MAY WHILE DYSPROSIUM HOLDS FIRM — JUNE RARE EARTH DIVERGENCE SIGNALS TRUE MAGNET GRADE COST PRESSURES
snippet: Mainrich International's June 2026 rare earth market update identifies a growing analytical gap between the neodymium-praseodymium headline and the heavy rare earth elements that actually determine whether EV and robotics manufacturers can source the magnet grades they specify: NdPr oxide corrected approximately 21% from its April 2026 benchmark to roughly $100/kg before recovering to $121.95/kg in June — but dysprosium held near $930/kg and terbium approached $4,030/kg in retail markets, continuing higher independently of the NdPr correction. The structural explanation: the NdFeB magnet grades specified for electric vehicle traction motors and humanoid robot actuators in high-temperature applications (H, SH, UH, EH series) require dysprosium or terbium additions for thermal coercivity that no cost-effective alternative currently provides. Dysprosium and terbium export availability is controlled by MOFCOM Announcement No. 18 licensing — a case-by-case government approval process that creates throughput constraints independent of China's overall rare earth production volume. MP Materials' first commercial magnet revenue in Q1 2026 represents a modest but real early indicator of Western supply chain self-sufficiency progress. For investors in TSXV and ASX rare earth developers, the June 2026 divergence reinforces the project-level screen: deposits with heavy rare earth content above 10% of TREO, and outside China's licensing jurisdiction, carry a supply security premium that the NdPr-focused rare earth market narrative is not yet pricing correctly.
